canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_1=(Γ,S,r,K,L,{γ_p}_{p∈(k,ℓ)},𝒢)∈𝒪_P, where Γ=(V,E) is a finite chemical reaction network, S is its stoichiometric matrix, r={r_A} is an admissible family of reaction-rate functions, K×L is the admissible parameter domain for reaction parameters k and conserved-quantity values ℓ, γ_p is the labeled buffering structure associated with parameter p, and 𝒢 is the induced set of elementary and generic robust-perfect-adaptation properties.
canonical_goal.target_object: A complete topological characterization of kinetics-independent robust perfect adaptation in finite deterministic chemical reaction systems: for every finite reaction network Γ=(V,E) with reactions e_A:∑_i s_{iA}v_i→∑_i t_{iA}v_i, stoichiometric matrix S with entries S_{iA}=t_{iA}−s_{iA}, deterministic dynamics d x/dt=S r(x;k), and conserved-quantity constraints d^{(ᾱ)}·x̄=ℓ_{ᾱ} for a basis {d^{(ᾱ)}} of coker S={d∈ℝ^{|V|}:d^T S=0}, the kinetics-independent elementary robust-perfect-adaptation property for a parameter p∈{k_A:e_A∈E}∪{ℓ_{ᾱ}:d^{(ᾱ)}∈coker S} is exactly represented by the labeled buffering structure γ_p=(V_p,E_p∪E^+_p). Here V_p={v_i∈V:∂x̄_i/∂p≠0}, E_p={e_A∈E:∂r̄_A/∂p≠0}, E^+_p={e_C∈E\E_p: some reactant of e_C lies in V_p}, γ_p is output-complete because every reaction with at least one reactant in V_p lies in E_p∪E^+_p, and γ_p has influence index λ(γ_p)=−|V_p|+|E_p∪E^+_p|−dim({c∈ker S:supp(c)⊆E_p∪E^+_p})+dim(P^0_{γ_p}(coker S))=0. The represented RPA conclusion is that every species in V\V_p and every reaction in E\E_p has a steady-state value independent of p for every admissible kinetics preserving positivity of x̄, differentiability of r_A, asymptotic stability of the Jacobian restricted to fixed conserved quantities, and the rule that (∂r_A/∂x_i)|_{x=x̄} is nonzero exactly for reactants; generic RPA properties for a parameter subset 𝒫 are obtained by unioning the affected sets V_p and E_p over p∈𝒫 and taking the corresponding complements.
feasibility_constraints: Γ=(V,E) is finite; each reaction e_A∈E has the form e_A:∑_i s_{iA}v_i→∑_i t_{iA}v_i with s_{iA},t_{iA}∈ℤ_{≥0}; S_{iA}=t_{iA}−s_{iA}; if a chemical step is reversible, its reverse direction is represented as a separate reaction with reactants and products interchanged.

The concentration vector x(t)∈ℝ_{>0}^{|V|} satisfies d x/dt=S r(x;k), where r_A(x;k_A) is differentiable and depends on concentrations only through reactants of e_A; the extracted goal does not assume the mass-action special case r_A(x;k_A)=k_A∏_i x_i^{s_{iA}}.
A steady state (x̄,r̄) exists for each admissible (k,ℓ)∈K×L and satisfies S r̄=0 and d^{(ᾱ)}·x̄=ℓ_{ᾱ} for a basis {d^{(ᾱ)}} of coker S={d∈ℝ^{|V|}:d^T S=0}; ker S={c∈ℝ^{|E|}:S c=0}.

The steady state is asymptotically stable after conserved quantities are fixed: on the affine set {x:d^{(ᾱ)}·x=ℓ_{ᾱ} for all ᾱ}, the Jacobian matrix of d x/dt=S r(x;k) at x̄ is nonsingular and every eigenvalue has strictly negative real part.

All steady-state concentrations are positive, x̄_i(k,ℓ)>0 for every v_i∈V, and the kinetic support condition holds at x̄: (∂r_A/∂x_i)|_{x=x̄}≠0 if v_i is a reactant of e_A and (∂r_A/∂x_i)|_{x=x̄}=0 if v_i is not a reactant of e_A.

For a parameter p∈{k_A:e_A∈E}∪{ℓ_{ᾱ}:d^{(ᾱ)}∈coker S}, robust perfect adaptation of species v_i means ∂x̄_i/∂p=0 for every constant-in-time perturbation p↦p+δp that preserves positivity, differentiability, the reactant-support condition, and asymptotic stability; robust perfect adaptation of reaction e_A means ∂r̄_A/∂p=0 under the same perturbations.

A generic robust-perfect-adaptation property (𝒱,𝓔,𝒫) is feasible exactly when 𝒱⊆V, 𝓔⊆E, 𝒫⊆{k_A:e_A∈E}∪{ℓ_{ᾱ}:d^{(ᾱ)}∈coker S}, and for every p∈𝒫 every v_i∈𝒱 satisfies ∂x̄_i/∂p=0 and every e_A∈𝓔 satisfies ∂r̄_A/∂p=0 for all admissible kinetics preserving the assumptions.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^{(1)}={o_1: for every parameter p∈{k_A:e_A∈E}∪{ℓ_{ᾱ}:d^{(ᾱ)}∈coker S}, the affected sets V_p={v_i∈V:∂x̄_i/∂p≠0} and E_p={e_A∈E:∂r̄_A/∂p≠0} determine the supplemental set E^+_p={e_C∈E\E_p: some reactant of e_C lies in V_p}; the labeled subnetwork γ_p=(V_p,E_p∪E^+_p) is output-complete and satisfies λ(γ_p)=−|V_p|+|E_p∪E^+_p|−dim({c∈ker S:supp(c)⊆E_p∪E^+_p})+dim(P^0_{γ_p}(coker S))=0; every v_i∈V\V_p and every e_A∈E\E_p exhibits robust perfect adaptation with respect to p; if 𝒫 is any subset of admissible parameters, V_𝒫=⋃_{p∈𝒫}V_p and E_𝒫=⋃_{p∈𝒫}E_p give the generic RPA property (V\V_𝒫,E\E_𝒫,𝒫); and every generic kinetics-independent RPA property can be represented by such a union of elementary labeled buffering structures}.

robustness_scope.ambient_space: The environment family consists of finite deterministic chemical reaction systems Γ=(V,E) with stoichiometric matrix S, concentration dynamics d x/dt=S r(x;k), admissible domains (k,ℓ)∈K×L, positive asymptotically stable steady states (x̄,r̄), differentiable reaction-rate functions r_A(x;k_A) whose nonzero concentration derivatives at x̄ occur exactly for reactants of e_A, and constant-in-time perturbations p↦p+δp of either a reaction parameter k_A or a conserved-quantity value ℓ_{ᾱ} that preserve positivity, differentiability, support, and asymptotic stability.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: I_1 = { (Γ,S,r,K,L,p) : Γ=(V,E) is finite; S_{iA}=t_{iA}−s_{iA} for reactions e_A:∑_i s_{iA}v_i→∑_i t_{iA}v_i with s_{iA},t_{iA}∈ℤ_{≥0}; r={r_A} is differentiable; (∂r_A/∂x_i)|_{x=x̄}≠0 exactly when v_i is a reactant of e_A; x̄_i>0 for all i; the Jacobian of S r(x;k) restricted to fixed conserved quantities has only eigenvalues with strictly negative real part; (k,ℓ)∈K×L; p∈{k_A:e_A∈E}∪{ℓ_{ᾱ}:d^{(ᾱ)}∈coker S}; and p↦p+δp is constant in time and leaves these conditions true }.

claimed_subfamily.definition: For every finite Γ=(V,E), S, differentiable kinetics r, admissible domains K×L, positive asymptotically stable steady state (x̄,r̄), and parameter p∈{k_A:e_A∈E}∪{ℓ_{ᾱ}:d^{(ᾱ)}∈coker S}, and for every replacement r↦r′ by differentiable rate functions with the same reaction graph and the same reactant-support pattern at a positive asymptotically stable steady state, the zero-derivative RPA coordinates forced by a labeled buffering structure are unchanged: if γ_p=(V_p,E_p∪E^+_p) is output-complete and λ(γ_p)=0, then every v_i∈V\V_p satisfies ∂x̄_i/∂p=0 and every e_A∈E\E_p satisfies ∂r̄_A/∂p=0 both for r and for r′.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_2=(Γ,S,r,K,L,γ,𝓘_γ,𝓩_γ)∈𝒪_P, where Γ=(V,E) is a finite deterministic chemical reaction network, γ=(V_γ,E_γ∪Ê_γ) is an output-complete zero-influence-index buffering structure associated with an elementary or generic robust-perfect-adaptation property, 𝓘_γ is the finite set of integrator equations constructed for γ, and 𝓩_γ is the algebraic zero-deviation constraint obtained from 𝓘_γ at steady state.
canonical_goal.target_object: For every robust-perfect-adaptation property represented by an output-complete zero-influence-index buffering structure γ=(V_γ,E_γ∪E^+_γ), construct an embedded integral-feedback representation that realizes the same steady-state independence from parameters internal to γ. Order the species and reactions so that x=(x_1,x_2)^T and r=(r_1,r_2)^T, where subscript 1 denotes species and reactions in γ and subscript 2 denotes species and reactions outside γ, and partition S as [[S_{11},S_{12}],[S_{21},S_{22}]]. For any real matrix A, write A^+ for its Moore-Penrose inverse, defined as the unique matrix X satisfying A X A=A, X A X=X, (A X)^T=A X, and (X A)^T=X A. Define S′=S_{22}−S_{21}S_{11}^+S_{12}, Q=[−S_{21}S_{11}^+  I], C(γ)=ker S_{11}/(ker S)_{supp γ}, U=span{S_{21}c:c∈C(γ)}, P as the orthogonal projection onto U^⊥, P_1 as the projection onto supp(E_γ)∩(ker S_{11})^⊥, and P_2 as the projection onto supp(E_γ)∩(ker S_{21})^⊥. For each emergent conserved quantity d^{(ā)}=(d_1^{(ā)},0) satisfying d^{(ā)}S=(0,c_2^{(ā)}), the required finite integrator set is d(d^{(ā)}·x)/dt=c_2^{(ā)}·r_2(x_2), P Q dx/dt=P S′r_2(x_2), P_1S_{11}^+dx_1/dt=P_1(r_1+S_{11}^+S_{12}r_2), and P_2S_{21}^+dx_2/dt=P_2(r_1+S_{21}^+S_{22}r_2). At any positive asymptotically stable steady state, the left-hand sides vanish and the right-hand sides impose algebraic set-point constraints on external concentrations x_2 and regulated reaction rates that contain no reaction parameter k_A with e_A∈E_γ∪E^+_γ and no conserved-quantity perturbation supported only inside γ.
feasibility_constraints: Γ=(V,E) is finite; each reaction e_A∈E has the form e_A:∑_i s_{iA}v_i→∑_i t_{iA}v_i with s_{iA},t_{iA}∈ℤ_{≥0}; S_{iA}=t_{iA}−s_{iA}; x(t)∈ℝ_{>0}^{|V|} satisfies d x/dt=S r(x;k); r_A(x;k_A) is differentiable and has nonzero concentration derivative at x̄ exactly for reactants of e_A; a positive steady state (x̄,r̄) exists and satisfies S r̄=0 and d^{(ᾱ)}·x̄=ℓ_{ᾱ} for a basis {d^{(ᾱ)}} of coker S={d∈ℝ^{|V|}:d^T S=0}.

The steady state is asymptotically stable after conserved quantities are fixed: on the affine set {x:d^{(ᾱ)}·x=ℓ_{ᾱ} for all ᾱ}, the Jacobian matrix of d x/dt=S r(x;k) at x̄ is nonsingular and every eigenvalue has strictly negative real part.
γ=(V_γ,E_γ∪E^+_γ) is output-complete: every reaction with at least one reactant in V_γ belongs to E_γ∪E^+_γ; hence each external reaction rate in r_2 depends only on external concentrations x_2.

γ has zero influence index λ(γ)=−|V_γ|+|E_γ∪E^+_γ|−dim((ker S)_{supp γ})+dim(P^0_γ(coker S))=0, where ker S={c∈ℝ^{|E|}:S c=0}, (ker S)_{supp γ}={c∈ker S:supp(c)⊆E_γ∪E^+_γ}, coker S={d∈ℝ^{|V|}:d^T S=0}, and P^0_γ maps a species covector to its coordinates on V_γ.

The block partition S=[[S_{11},S_{12}],[S_{21},S_{22}]] is formed by ordering internal species/reactions in γ first and external species/reactions outside γ second; x=(x_1,x_2)^T and r=(r_1,r_2)^T follow the same ordering.

The vector spaces used in the integrator construction are finite dimensional and explicitly defined by C(γ)=ker S_{11}/(ker S)_{supp γ}, U=span{S_{21}c:c∈C(γ)}, D(γ)=coker S_{11}/D_{11}(γ), and D_{11}(γ)={d_1∈coker S_{11}: there exists d_2 such that (d_1,d_2)∈coker S}; for any matrix A, ker A={z:A z=0} and coker A={z:z^T A=0}.

The constructed integrator equations are evaluated only for trajectories and constant-in-time perturbations that preserve the positive asymptotically stable steady state, differentiability of the rate functions, and the reactant-support condition; the claim is not made for unstable systems or for kinetic functions whose nonzero concentration-derivative pattern differs from the reaction graph.

claimed_subfamily.definition: For every finite deterministic chemical reaction system Γ=(V,E) with stoichiometric matrix S, dynamics d x/dt=S r(x;k), differentiable reaction-rate functions whose nonzero concentration derivatives occur exactly for reactants, a positive asymptotically stable steady state satisfying S r̄=0 and d^{(ᾱ)}·x̄=ℓ_{ᾱ}, and an output-complete γ=(V_γ,E_γ∪E^+_γ) with λ(γ)=0, the integrator equations constructed from S_{11},S_{12},S_{21},S_{22}, the Moore-Penrose inverse A^+ of each required matrix A, the emergent-cycle quotient C(γ)=ker S_{11}/(ker S)_{supp γ}, and the emergent-conserved-quantity quotient D(γ)=coker S_{11}/D_{11}(γ) have steady-state right-hand sides depending only on external rates r_2(x_2), structural matrices, and conserved quantities not supported solely inside γ; therefore the resulting steady-state values of x_2 and the regulated rates are independent of reaction parameters k_A for e_A∈E_γ∪E^+_γ and of conserved-quantity perturbations supported only inside γ for every admissible kinetics preserving positivity, support, and asymptotic stability.

methodological_claim.target_object: The paper claims a computational linear-algebraic enumeration method for identifying all labeled buffering structures of a finite deterministic chemical reaction network. The input is Γ=(V,E), the stoichiometric matrix S, bases {c^{(α)}} of ker S={c∈ℝ^{|E|}:S c=0} and {d^{(ᾱ)}} of coker S={d∈ℝ^{|V|}:d^T S=0}, and the binary reactant-support pattern σ_{iA}=1 exactly when v_i is a reactant of e_A. Construct the structural response matrix A using S, the two bases, and generic nonzero entries at exactly the positions where σ_{iA}=1; compute A^{-1}; define the species-sensitivity matrix X_{iA}=(A^{-1})_{iA}; define the reaction-sensitivity matrix R_{BA}=∑_α c_B^{(α)}(A^{-1})_{αA}; set V_A={v_i∈V:X_{iA}≠0} and E_A={e_B∈E:R_{BA}≠0}; set E^+_A={e_C∈E\E_A: some reactant of e_C lies in V_A}; and output γ_A=(V_A,E_A∪E^+_A) for each reaction-parameter label A, with the analogous construction for conserved-quantity labels. This is a methodological claim about how the characterization is enumerated, not an additional end-state goal over biological networks.

source_span.verbatim: This study introduces a framework for characterizing RPA mechanisms in deterministic chemical reaction networks, utilizing topological invariants to systematically identify all structural configurations that enable robustness.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated paper goal is the conjunction of two formal propositions. First, for every finite deterministic chemical reaction system Γ=(V,E) with d x/dt=S r(x;k), conserved-quantity constraints d^{(ᾱ)}·x̄=ℓ_{ᾱ}, positive asymptotic stability, and the reactant-support condition (∂r_A/∂x_i)|_{x=x̄}≠0 exactly for reactants v_i of e_A, every kinetics-independent elementary robust-perfect-adaptation property under p↦p+δp is equivalent to a labeled output-complete zero-influence-index subnetwork γ_p=(V_p,E_p∪E^+_p), and every generic robust-perfect-adaptation property is obtained by unioning elementary affected sets over a parameter subset. Second, for every such γ_p, there is a finite set of integrator equations whose steady-state zero conditions determine the regulated external concentrations and rates without internal parameters of γ_p.
